text: The from queue, the to queue, the from owner and the to owner of a transfer, the transfer reason on a manual transfer and the trigger event code are held in decision_log_entry.actions (DF-DEC-014), the JSONB field that records the action and its result; LOV-DECISION holds the decision codes of the FSD (D-codes, X-codes and access events).
why: The entry must explain the transfer with identifiers only, T3.1 offers no column for them, and actions is the only JSONB field that describes what was done; a code list must exist before a code can be refused.
read: TSD P7 Decision center and log v2 T3.1 and T3.2; FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 A2.2 and A2.8; API Specification v4 DecisionLogEntry
confirm: Solution architect, P7 and the data steward
impact: The field names inside the JSONB shape the read and the screen; no code branch changes, and a later column is a migration of the store story.

text: The model read is GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/rule-models/{packageCode}/{version}, with the package code and the version label as path parameters, answering the compiled model, its SHA-256 checksum and its rows in row order, and refusing a version whose state is not IN_FORCE or whose checksum does not match.
why: Architecture v5 names the read and the Temporal and Drools design names what the owning service does with it; the API document has not caught up with either.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14; Temporal and Drools Design v1 slide 15; API Specification v4 appendix T-A
impact: Four owning services consume this path; a rename after the event is published is a contract change for all of them.

text: MSG-P7-009 and MSG-P7-012 are cited by ID and by the field or the entry each one names; the sentence is read from the message catalogue at run time and is not written into this story's code.
why: No source gives the text, and the message ID with the field it names is a stable key that survives a wording change.
read: FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 A2.2 and A2.8; API Specification v4 /decision-log description
impact: None on behaviour; the rendering follows the catalogue.

text: For a transfer, an unavailable ledger store is answered to the caller that waits on the seal with 503 and MSG-P7-003, and the record otherwise stays on rwb.decision-record.v1 and is appended when the store returns; the transfer itself is not undone, because its local record committed in rwb-case.
why: Two sources read the central ledger two ways, and a transfer is not on the strict list of points of no return in the Temporal design.
read: FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 A2.1 and A2.8; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-UNI-39; Temporal and Drools Design v1 slide 28
confirm: RW-RISK and the solution architect, P7
impact: Decides whether a transfer can complete while the central ledger is down, and therefore which callers can ever see MSG-P7-003 for a transfer.
